title: Finance & Legal: Budgeting, Contracts, Procurement, Revenue Recognition, and Billing Policy
author: Priya Patel
content:
Purpose
-------
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's core finance and legal operating policies for budgeting and forecasting, contracts and legal review, procurement approvals and procedures, and revenue recognition & billing. It is intended for finance, legal, procurement, product, and engineering managers who participate in planning, purchasing, contracting, and revenue operations.

Scope
-----
Applies to all Redwood entities and product lines. Covers: 
- Annual and quarterly budgeting cadence and owners
- Rolling forecasting methodology and frequency
- Standard procurement workflow and approval thresholds
- Contract lifecycle, templates, and legal review SLAs
- Revenue recognition principles (SaaS, usage, one-time fees) and billing operating procedures

Key Definitions
---------------
- CAPEX vs OPEX: Capital expenditures (capitalizable hardware/software) vs operating expenses. Finance will classify per capitalization policy.
- ARR: Annualized run rate based on contracted recurring revenue.
- Deferred revenue: Cash received for which revenue is recognized over a future period.
- Net-30: Standard payment term meaning payment due 30 days after invoice date.

1) Budgeting and Forecasting
---------------------------
Overview
: Redwood runs an annual budgeting process with quarterly re-forecasts and a rolling 12-month forecast maintained by Finance. Budgets align to product, infra, GTM, and corporate functional plans.

Cadence and Timeline
: 
1. Annual planning kickoff: mid-October (Finance issues templates and targets)
2. Department submissions due: first week of November
3. Leadership review & consolidation: November–December
4. Final board-submitted budget: mid-December
5. Quarterly re-forecast windows: end of January, April, July, October

Owners and Responsibilities
- Finance: overall process owner, budget consolidation, variance reporting, and capital approval coordination.
- Product & Engineering Managers: submit resource and headcount requests, project cost forecasts.
- GTM Leaders: revenue targets, go-to-market spend requests.
- People Ops: headcount planning and salary assumptions.

Assumptions and Drivers
: Each submission must include explicit assumptions for headcount, avg. salary, hiring cadence, cloud/GPU spend, model licensing costs, and expected customer growth by segment. All material assumptions must be captured in the submission workbook.

Forecasting Methodology
: Rolling 12-month forecast updated monthly for the revenue engine and infrastructure spend; product and headcount forecasts updated quarterly unless triggered by major changes. Scenario planning (base, upside, downside) is maintained for major revenue line items.

Variance Reporting and KPIs
: Finance will publish a monthly variance pack covering: actuals vs plan, burn rate, runway (if applicable), ARR movement, gross margin by product, and top 10 drivers of variance. Ownership of corrective actions rests with the owning functional lead.

Capital Requests and Approval
: Requests to capitalize hardware (>= $50,000) or multi-year software must use the CapEx request form and be approved by Finance and the CFO. Minor capitalizable items between $10k–$50k require director-level approval plus Finance pre-approval.

2) Contracts and Legal Process
-----------------------------
Purpose
: Ensure consistent, compliant contracting practices that protect Redwood while enabling business velocity.

Contract Types and Templates
- Master Services Agreement (MSA) — standard customer template (legal_owner: Legal).
- Data Processing Agreement (DPA) — for customers with personal data requirements.
- Vendor Master Agreement (VMA) — for suppliers, includes security and SLA language.
- Professional Services Statement of Work (SOW) — for time & materials or fixed-fee engagements.

Contract Review SLA and Routing
- First-pass legal review SLA: 3 business days for standard contracts
- Extended review SLA: 7–10 business days for custom/high-risk terms
- Routing: Contracts are submitted via the Contract Intake Form (digital) and routed to Legal with Finance cc for revenue-impacting contracts.

Approval Matrix
- < $5k (non-recurring vendor spend): Manager approval
- $5k–$50k: Director approval + Finance notification
- $50k–$250k or multi-year commitments: VP approval + Finance sign-off
- > $250k or strategic vendor/customer terms or material SLA liability: CFO + Legal approval
- Any contract that modifies revenue recognition (e.g., extended terms, rebates, bundling): Must be reviewed by Revenue Ops (Finance) and Legal prior to signature.

Key Clauses to Confirm
- Ownership of IP, indemnities, limitation of liability (cap at 1x contract value unless escalated), data security and breach notification, termination rights, and export controls. For customers in regulated industries, include the standard Redwood regulatory addendum.

Contract Retention and Registry
: All fully executed contracts must be uploaded to the Contract Registry (Legal's DocStore). Retention schedule: 7 years for commercial contracts, longer if required by customer/regulation. Finance maintains copies of revenue-impacting contracts.

3) Procurement Procedures
-------------------------
Objective
: Control spend, maintain vendor governance, and accelerate purchasing for low-risk items.

Procurement Workflow
1. Requester submits Purchase Request in Procurement Portal including business justification, GL code, and estimated amount.
2. Manager approval per thresholds below.
3. Procurement team sources quotes (competitive quotes required for $50k+).
4. Legal review for vendor terms if vendor agreement is required.
5. Finance validates budget availability and issues PO (where applicable).
6. Vendor onboarding and security review for vendors with access to customer data.

Approval Thresholds and Controls
- Purchase Requisition Thresholds:
  - < $5,000: Manager approval sufficient; expect standard P-card or PO as appropriate.
  - $5,000–$50,000: Director approval + Procurement notification.
  - $50,000–$250,000: VP approval + Procurement competitive sourcing (>=2 bids).
  - > $250,000: CFO approval + Procurement-led RFP and Legal review.
- Purchase Orders: Required for all vendor payments > $10,000 and for capital spend.
- Competitive Sourcing: Required for purchases >= $50,000 unless documented exception approved by Procurement Lead.

Vendor Risk and Security Review
: Any vendor or supplier that will access customer data, infrastructure, or receive guarded IP must complete a security questionnaire and be reviewed by Security & Procurement before onboarding. High-risk vendors require SOC2/ISO27001 or equivalent evidence.

Payment Methods
: Preferred flow is vendor invoiced to Finance for payment. For low-dollar, time-sensitive purchases, company P-cards are allowed with monthly reconciliation. Wire transfers and ACH follow treasury controls.

4) Revenue Recognition and Billing Policies
-----------------------------------------
Principles
: Redwood recognizes revenue in accordance with GAAP / ASC 606 principles. Finance (RevOps) is responsible for policy interpretation and maintaining deferred revenue schedules. This section summarizes common scenarios used by teams.

Recurring SaaS Subscriptions
- Recognition: Ratably over the subscription term starting on the service commencement date.
- Example: Annual prepay of $120,000 recognized at $10,000/month over 12 months.
- Upgrades/Downgrades: Pro-rated recognition adjustments applied on change dates.

Usage-Based Revenue
- Recognition: Recognize in the period the usage occurs. Customers billed monthly in arrears unless different terms are negotiated.

One-Time Professional Services and Setup Fees
- If services are distinct and have standalone value: Recognize upon delivery/completion.
- If services are not distinct and are integral to the contract (i.e., create or modify the service), defer and recognize over the term of the related subscription. Default deferral period is 12 months unless contract-specific term dictates otherwise.

Bundled Contracts and Multiple Performance Obligations
- Allocation: Apply contract-specific allocation using relative standalone selling price (SSP) methodology. When bundles combine subscription + services, finance will allocate consideration and recognize per obligation.

Contract Modifications
- Material contract modifications (term extension, material price concessions, rebates) are reviewed by RevOps and Legal to determine treatment (prospective vs. cumulative catch-up).

Billing Operations
- Standard Terms: Net-30 for most customers. Exceptions (Net-45, Net-60, upfront prepay) require Sales + Finance approval.
- Invoice cadence: monthly in arrears for usage and subscription unless annual prepay is contracted.
- Tax: Billing team will apply tax rules per customer jurisdiction; Sales must capture VAT/GST IDs where applicable.
- Late Payments: Late fee of 1.5% per month after 30 days past due (subject to local laws). Collections escalation: 30 days (reminder), 60 days (account manager outreach), 90 days (legal collections; withhold service or suspend account as per contract).

Credit and Billing Disputes
- Dispute process: Customer must raise invoice disputes within 30 days of invoice date. Sales/Finance will create dispute ticket; Finance provides provisional crediting only when dispute validated.

Deferred Revenue and Reporting
- Finance maintains a deferred revenue schedule and posts journal entries monthly. Quarterly reviews reconcile deferred balances to executed contracts and billing.
- Revenue Cutover: For new product lines or material policy changes, RevOps must coordinate with Audit and Legal to validate approach prior to external reporting.

5) Finance Controls and Auditability
----------------------------------
Segregation of Duties
: Procurement/PO creation, vendor invoice approval, and payment execution are segregated to limit fraud risk.

Audit and Evidence
: Finance and Legal retain contract evidence, invoices, and change orders in the corporate document repository. Audit-ready packs (revenue bridge, deferred revenue rollforwards, contract listing) are prepared quarterly.

Key Metrics for Monitoring
- DSO (Days Sales Outstanding) target: <45 days
- Revenue recognition accuracy target: >99% (quarterly reconciliations)
- Procurement cycle time target: <7 business days for <50k purchases

Appendix A — Example Approval Matrix (table)
| Amount | Approval Required | Notes |
|--------|-------------------|-------|
| < $5k   | Manager           | P-card allowed |
| $5k–$50k | Director         | Procurement notified |
| $50k–$250k | VP            | 2+ quotes; Procurement involvement |
| > $250k | CFO + Legal       | RFP recommended; executive review |

Appendix B — Revenue Recognition Examples
- Annual prepaid subscription: $24,000 prepay for 24 months -> recognize $1,000/month.
- One-time setup that is integral to subscription: $12,000 -> defer and recognize $1,000/month over 12 months by default.
- Usage billing: 10,000 tokens billed at month end -> recognized in the month usage occurred.

FAQ and Exceptions
------------------
- Q: Who can sign contracts?
  A: Authorized signatories are the CEO and CFO for customer contracts; delegated signers (VP-level) may sign up to $250k where pre-approved in writing.
- Q: What if a contract needs accelerated legal review?
  A: Use the legal expedite queue; Legal will attempt same-day triage for time-sensitive deals but SLA is not guaranteed.
